description: Declared with `only`. — this silently disables every other test in the file, so the suite passes while almost nothing runs
`return` inside the clause that runs on the way out — it replaces whatever the block was leaving with, so a failure raised in the body disappears and nothing records that it happened
Calls itself 1 times per invocation with no memo in sight. — nothing can stop the recursion, so the first call exhausts the stack

`rows` is changed while it is being walked. — the iteration and the mutation disagree about what remains, so elements are skipped or visited twice depending on where the change lands
`case 1:` runs on into the arm below — the arm below also runs, and nothing here says whether that was intended
`(kind === "a")` is asked twice in one chain — the second branch cannot be reached, so whatever it was written to do has never run
Both arms of this branch do the same thing. — the decision changes nothing, so either it is not a decision or one branch was meant to differ
`count` is compared against itself. — the result is decided before the comparison runs, so either it does nothing or one side was meant to be a different expression
`found = a + b` assigns where a condition is expected. — it reads as a comparison and behaves as an assignment, so an accidental assignment is easy to miss in review
This catch clause has an empty body. — the failure is swallowed silently, so it first appears as wrong data elsewhere, with nothing in the logs to connect the two
This statement cannot run: the block always returns before reaching it. — this code cannot run, so whatever it was written to do is not happening
`loadOne` answers later and nothing takes the answer. — nothing waits for it and nothing observes its failure, so a failure surfaces elsewhere with no link to what started it

`expect(add(1, 1)).toBe(add(1, 1));` has the same expression on both sides — it holds the code to whatever the code already does, so it keeps passing through every change, including a change that breaks the behaviour

`sumTo` calls itself once with `n` one smaller each time, so the stack it needs is O(n) deep. — every level keeps its stack frame until the last one returns, so an input larger than the stack allows ends in a stack overflow that tests on small inputs never reach

`indexOfItem` is called on every pass of a loop over `items` and itself takes time in `items`. O(n²): loop :12 → indexOfItem O(n) :1 → loop :2. — the callee does work in proportion to a collection on every pass of the loop, so the total grows with the product of the two sizes, and with the square of the size when they are one collection, although the caller shows only one loop
`RegExp` runs on every pass of the loop. — the same pattern is parsed and compiled on every pass when once would do, and compiling is the expensive half of matching
Declared with `skip`. — a skipped test reports success while the behaviour it names goes unchecked
Parameter `value` is reassigned inside the function. — the caller's value changes without the call site saying so, which is hard to find when it turns out to be wrong
`@ts-ignore` turns off a check that covers this code. — a check that would have caught the next mistake here has been turned off, and the comment that turns it off outlives the reason for it

`rqx-ignore with no reason` turns off a check that covers this code. — the waiver is refused and the finding still counts, because a waiver that needs no justification allows a rule to be switched off one line at a time
the handler is only `throw error;` — it reads as a decision about the failure and makes none, and in languages that rebuild the stack trace on rethrow it loses the original
`warmTheCache` runs when the file is loaded. — it runs before any caller has asked for anything, in whatever order the imports resolve, and nothing can prevent it
`CsvWriter` is built by the object that holds it. — nothing can be substituted for them, so every test of the owner has to set up the real collaborator and everything behind it
The import `Far` is declared and never read. — it makes the file appear to depend on something it does not use, and the dependency survives every search for who needs that module

`0.1` is compared for exact equality — a binary float rarely equals the decimal a person wrote, so a branch that depends on it is decided by rounding and not by the value

`totalLength` runs on every pass of the loop. — the call returns the same answer on every pass, so the loop pays its cost once per pass where once in total would do

`Promise.all` starts one piece of work per element with nothing limiting how many run at once. — the number of requests in flight equals the size of the collection, so a large input exhausts connections, memory or the other side's rate limit

`pageSizes` gains an entry for every distinct key it is given and is never trimmed. — it holds an entry for every distinct key the program has ever been given, so memory grows with the variety of the input for as long as the process runs
`latch.lock` runs on every pass of the loop. — each pass pays to acquire and release the same lock, and other threads can only interleave at those points instead of waiting once for the whole loop
`<expression>.sort` runs on every pass of the loop. — every pass after the first sorts input that is already sorted, at a cost of n log n each time

`entries.shift` runs on every pass of the loop. — the call costs time proportional to the size of the collection on every pass, so the loop grows with the product of its own length and the collection's
`rows.splice` runs on every pass of the loop. — the call costs time proportional to the size of the collection on every pass, so the loop grows with the product of its own length and the collection's

`flat` runs on every pass of the loop. — each step copies everything gathered so far, so building a result of n items touches about half of n squared items

`reader.read` runs on every pass of the loop. — each pass waits for the previous one to finish, so work that could overlap runs end to end and the loop takes as long as all of its waits added together
`fetch` runs on every pass of the loop. — every pass pays a round trip, so listing a hundred rows makes a hundred and one requests and the page waits for the sum of them
